349385.title: Hocquard–Lajou–Lužar conjecture on nine-coloring bridgeless subcubic graphs
349385.statement:
Let $G$ be a **bridgeless subcubic graph**, so every vertex has degree at most $3$ and $G$ has no bridges. Let the Wagner graph be the $8$-vertex Möbius ladder, and let $K_{3,3}$ with one edge subdivided denote the graph obtained from the complete bipartite graph $K_{3,3}$ by subdividing one edge.

**Hocquard–Lajou–Lužar conjecture.** If $G$ is not isomorphic to the Wagner graph or to $K_{3,3}$ with one edge subdivided, then $G$ admits a strong $9$-edge-coloring.

The conjecture is motivated by computational evidence and is stated as a proposed strengthening of known bounds for bridgeless subcubic graphs.

349385.primary_locations: 2101.04768 §1, Conjectures 5.3–5.4; strong coloring is proper coloring of the square of the line graph

Completed 3000 configuration-model attempts each at orders 14,16,18,20,24; eligible counts 337,351,373,385,414, all 9-colorable by exact DSATUR. Order-30 run hit CPU cap; no completed coverage claim for it. Source reports exhaustive evidence through order 18 for its stronger girth-5 assertion.
349385.remaining_gap: No counterexample. Need canonical subcubic generation beyond the authors range or a structural coloring theorem. Disconnected unions of an excluded component are a formulation issue, not credited.

349399.title: Same-singularity-type conjecture for similarly shaped partitions
349399.statement:
Let $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ be $r$-dimensional partitions of lengths $l_1$ and $l_2$, respectively. Suppose that they have similar shapes and

$$
\operatorname{ex.dim}_{I_{\lambda_1}}\operatorname{Hilb}^{l_1}(\mathbb{A}^r)=\operatorname{ex.dim}_{I_{\lambda_2}}\operatorname{Hilb}^{l_2}(\mathbb{A}^r).
$$

**Same-singularity-type conjecture.** Then the germs

$$
\operatorname{Hilb}^{l_1}(\mathbb{A}^3)_{Z_{I_{\lambda_1}}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{Hilb}^{l_2}(\mathbb{A}^3)_{Z_{I_{\lambda_2}}}
$$

are singularities of the same type.

This generalizes the observed agreement between local models for similarly shaped partitions. The statement is based on examples and computations in the paper and remains open.
349399.review_depth: primary conjecture and adjacent local models read
349399.primary_locations: 2101.05236 Conjecture 4.32, §4.5.3; Proposition 4.30; extra dimension and Haiman neighborhoods
349399.mathematical_attempt: The source explains similar shapes informally via relative positions of minimal monomial generators, and defines same type using chains of smooth morphisms. The r-dimensional-to-A^3 notation is inherited. Verified small models and tripod cases do not imply general analytic equivalence.
349399.remaining_gap: No faithful canonical enumeration of the informal shape relation or all-order local-ring invariant implemented. No finite numerical coverage claimed; no literal formal endpoint.

349403.title: Arithmetical structures conjecture on extremal graph orders
349403.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with $n$ vertices. For a graph $H$, let $\mathcal{A}(H)$ denote its set of arithmetical structures, and let $|\mathcal{A}(H)|$ be its cardinality. Let $P_n$ and $K_n$ be the path and complete graph, respectively, on $n$ vertices.

**Arithmetical structures conjecture.**

$$
\big|\mathcal{A}(P_n)\big|\leq \big|\mathcal{A}(G)\big|\leq \big|\mathcal{A}(K_n)\big|.
$$

This conjecture predicts that among simple graphs on $n$ vertices, the path minimizes and the complete graph maximizes the number of arithmetical structures. The paper presents computational evidence for the claim; no resolution is supplied here.

349435.title: The girth conjecture for the hypergraphs D'(k,q)
349435.statement: Let $D'(k,q)$ be the hypergraph defined in the paper, and let its girth be the length of its shortest cycle. **Girth conjecture for $D'(k,q)$.** The hypergraph $D'(k,q)$ has girth at least $k+4$ if $k$ is even, and $k+5$ if $k$ is odd. Proving this would yield lower bounds on the extremal number of hypergraph suspensions of even cycles via the construction developed in the paper. The conjecture is motivated by computational evidence, but no resolution is given here.

350308.title: The Kreweras interval conjecture for tree-like chord diagrams
350308.statement:
Let $C_n(T_{\geqslant 3},B_{\geqslant 3})$ be the set of connected chord diagrams of size $n$ avoiding all top and bottom cycles of size at least $3$, and let $\textnormal{Int}(\mathcal{L}^{K}_{n})$ denote the intervals of the Kreweras lattice. **The Kreweras interval conjecture.** There is a bijection

$$
C_n(T_{\geqslant 3},B_{\geqslant 3})\cong \textnormal{Int}(\mathcal{L}^{K}_{n}),
$$

and both sets have cardinality $\frac{1}{2n+1}\binom{3n}{n}$. This conjecture proposes a Catalan-poset interpretation for these tree diagrams; it is based on manual computations for small $n$, and its general validity remains open.
350308.review_depth: primary conjecture; same-author thesis exact proposition and corollary read; exact enumeration
350308.primary_locations: 2104.02296 Conjecture 7.8; chord-thesis Proposition 3.0.1 and Corollary 3.0.2 pp.50–51

Thesis explicitly attributes the enumeration to Leroux–Miloudi and Dulucq–Penaud and says the explicit bijection to Kreweras intervals remains open. Exact recursive matching enumeration at n=2 and n=8 confirms the offset.
350308.remaining_gap: Literal n-versus-n+1 failure is zero-credit correction. Corrected existence of an arbitrary finite bijection follows from the old equal cardinalities; an interesting nice bijection is not the literal existence question. No new discovery.

350631.title: The vanishing conjecture for second uberhomology
350631.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple and connected graph. Let $\mathbb{H}^2(G)$ denote the second uberhomology defined in the paper, namely the homology whose generators are edges with both endpoints coloured white, arranged over the poset $\mathbb{Z}_2^{|V(G)|}$ with differentials induced by inclusion.

**Vanishing conjecture for second uberhomology.**

$$
\mathbb{H}^2(G)=0.
$$

This was suggested by computations with the authors' program for simple connected graphs; no proof or disproof is supplied in the source.
350631.review_depth: source exact definition and Conjecture 8.3 read; ordinary decomposition and edge-cube diagnostic

350631.mathematical_attempt: Each white-white edge supplies a Boolean-cube summand on the n-2 remaining vertices; maps adding an endpoint go to zero, maps adding other vertices preserve that edge. This cube is contractible for n>2, while at n=2 it has one nonzero generator. Edge-cube ranks over F2 are checked for n=2..12.

350861.title: The shifted generalized forest submatrix Hankel-total positivity conjecture
350861.statement: Let $G'(p,q,\gamma,z)=\mathsf{F}(p,q,0,0,\gamma,0,0,z)\operatorname{diag}(((pq\gamma)^{n(n-1)/2})_{n\geq0})$, and let $G'_n(x;p,q,\gamma,z)=\sum_{k=0}^n g'_{n,k}(p,q,\gamma,z)x^k$. **The shifted generalized forest submatrix conjecture.** The polynomial sequence $(G'_n(x;p+1,q+1,\gamma+1,z))_{n\geq0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive jointly in $p,q,\gamma,z,x$. The unmodified two-parameter specialization is not even $\mathrm{TP}_2$, while the diagonal modification and unit shifts are supported by computation; the conjecture remains open.

351086.title: The trinomial constructions of iso-dual polycyclic codes
351086.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and consider the indicated trinomial-associated polycyclic codes. **Iso-dual construction conjecture.** The following codes are isodual:

- If $q$ is a power of an odd prime, a code associated with $x^{2m}\pm 2cx^m+c^2$ and generated by $g(x)=\pm x^m\pm c$.
- If $q$ is a power of $2$, a code associated with $x^{2m}+a^2x^{2i}+b^2$ and generated by $g(x)=x^m+ax^i+b$.

These are proposed on the basis of preceding results and computational evidence; the source does not provide a resolution of the conjectured constructions.

351107.title: Universality of critical exponents on transitive graphs of polynomial growth
351107.statement: Let Bernoulli percolation and lattice trees be defined on transitive graphs of polynomial growth, and let the **volume-growth dimension** denote the dimension governing the graph's polynomial volume growth. **Universality conjecture.** The critical exponents describing Bernoulli percolation and lattice trees on transitive graphs of polynomial growth are each determined by the volume-growth dimension of the graph. For $k=1$, this extends the positivity conjecture of Goulden and Jackson; the conjecture has been tested computationally in several small cases, but remains open in general.

351354.title: The Lyndon-permutation dimension conjecture for feasible regions
351354.statement:
Let $P_k$ be the set of permutons, and let $clP_k$ denote the feasible region of pattern densities for permutations of size at most $k$. Let $\mathcal{L}_k$ be the set of Lyndon permutations of size at most $k$.

**Lyndon-permutation dimension conjecture.** The feasible region $clP_k$ contains an open ball of dimension $|\mathcal{L}_k|$.

The previously known lower bound came from the set of $\oplus$-indecomposable permutations, while an algebraic-variety argument gives the upper bound $|\mathcal{L}_k|$. The conjecture asserts that this upper bound is attained; the source notes that computations confirm it for small $k$.

351520.title: Primitive-matrix generation conjecture for integral vectors
351520.statement:
Let $v$ be an $n$-dimensional integral vector whose entries are all nonzero modulo $p$. Suppose that

$$
v^{\mathsf T}e\equiv 0\pmod{p},\qquad v^{\mathsf T}v\equiv 0\pmod{p}.
$$
Here $e$ denotes the all-one vector, and a vector **generates a primitive matrix** when it occurs as the relevant generating vector for a primitive matrix in the paper's construction. **Primitive-matrix generation conjecture.** The following hold: (i) if $n\leq 8$, then $v$ can always generate some primitive matrix; and (ii) if $n\geq 2p+1$, then $v$ cannot generate any primitive matrix. The conjecture is motivated by computational experiments on graphs in the family studied in the paper; the stated criteria are proposed for further study and are not proved in the source.

351631.title: The Suzuki-group construction has edge-girth parameter q-1
351631.statement:
Let $q=2^{2e+1}$, and let $\mathcal G_q(V,E)$ be the graph constructed from the biaffine-plane and Suzuki-group construction. An $egr(v,k,g,\lambda)$-graph is an edge-girth-regular graph with order $v$, degree $k$, girth $g$, and each edge lying in exactly $\lambda$ cycles of length $g$.

**The edge-girth conjecture.** The family of graphs $\mathcal G_q(V,E)$ is a family of

$$
egr(q(q^2+1),q,5,q-1)
$$

-graphs.

The construction is already known to give graphs with the displayed order, degree, and girth, while the conjecture asserts that every edge lies in exactly $q-1$ pentagons. It was checked computationally for $q=8$; the general case remains open.
351631.review_depth: primary coset-geometry construction, girth proof and conjecture read
351631.mathematical_attempt: Vertices are cosets of G1=E_q:C_(q-1) in Sz(q); edges are cosets of G2=D_(2(q-1)), with intersection incidence. Source establishes order q(q²+1), degree q, girth5 and lambda>=q-1 using rank-three residues; q=8 tested in Magma. That lower-bound geometry does not exclude additional pentagons.
351631.remaining_gap: No authenticated explicit subgroup embedding/coset labeling model was built without Magma/GAP. No q=32 search claimed. Need that finite model or a group-theoretic count proving all pentagons come from source rank-three residues.

381804.title: The almost-all-trees lower-bound conjecture for small Laplacian eigenvalues
381804.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with diameter $d$, and let $m_T[0,1)$ denote the number of Laplacian eigenvalues of $T$ less than $1$. **Almost-all-trees lower-bound conjecture.** Almost all trees have at least

$$
\left\lceil\frac{d+1}{3}\right\rceil+1
$$

Laplacian eigenvalues less than $1$. This would improve the general lower bound by one for asymptotically almost all trees. The statement is presented as a consequence of the conjecture that the proportion of trees attaining the existing lower bound tends to zero; the supplied text also says that this conjecture was confirmed independently by Sin and by Jacobs, Oliveira and Trevisan.

381807.title: The commuting-Toffoli characterization of third-level permutation gates
381807.statement: Let $\mathcal{CH}_k$ denote the $k$th level of the qubit Clifford hierarchy, and let a permutation gate be a unitary that permutes the computational-basis states. A **Clifford permutation** is a permutation gate belonging to the Clifford group, and a **Toffoli gate** is a doubly controlled bit flip, denoted $C^2(X)$. **The commuting-Toffoli conjecture.** A permutation is in $\mathcal{CH}_3$ if and only if it can be written as a circuit of commuting Toffoli gates, possibly preceded and followed by Clifford permutations. The forward implication is open; the reverse implication follows from the results described in the paper.
381807.review_depth: primary exact theorem and rejection proof read
381807.mathematical_attempt: He–Robitaille–Tan explicitly refute the commuting-Toffoli characterization. Pairwise commuting controlled-NOT gates are mismatch-free and therefore semi-Clifford up to Clifford permutations, whereas their seven-qubit permutation is not.
381807.remaining_gap: Already public in October 2024; no new numerical search or upstream Lean certification needed.

381808.title: The inverse-closure conjecture for permutation gates in the Clifford hierarchy
381808.statement: Let $\mathcal{CH}_k$ denote the $k$th level of the qubit Clifford hierarchy, and let $\pi$ be a permutation gate on the computational-basis states. **The inverse-closure conjecture.** If $\pi$ is in $\mathcal{CH}_k$, then its adjoint $\pi^\dagger$ is also in $\mathcal{CH}_k$. This is a natural closure question for permutation gates in the hierarchy, and its resolution is not established by the supplied text.
